sentences.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption examines governance challenges in local Aboriginal land councils and how accountability and regulation could be improved.
sentences.support: This report examines those challenges and the factors contributing to them.

sentences.text: It considers member participation, board capacity, conflicts of interest and oversight by the NSW Aboriginal Land Council and the Registrar.
sentences.support: Member participation rates at meetings in many LALCs are low

sentences.text: The Commission identifies low participation, limits to board training and overlapping regulatory functions as barriers to effective accountability.
sentences.support: there is an overlap between regulators such as NSWALC and the Registrar

sentences.text: The Commission makes 11 improvement suggestions covering member engagement, governance rules, board skills, regulatory coordination, resources and oversight of council entities.
sentences.support: The following suggestions for improvement are made in this report.

findings.quote: There is scope to strengthen the effectiveness of both the Registrar and NSWALC in overseeing LALCs.
There is potential to strengthen members’ ability to hold the leadership of LALCs accountable.

notes: The report labels its 11 proposed actions suggestions for improvement. Executive summary includes the suggestions list through PDF page 9; complaints described in the introduction are not findings.
